source.title: SPAM: Spike-Aware Adam with Momentum Reset for Stable LLM Training
source.authors: Tian-Jin Huang; Zi-Quan Zhu; Gao-Jie Jin; Lu Liu; Zhang-Yang Wang; Shi-Wei Liu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies gradient spikes and optimizer performance in LLM training. It does not test the listed claims about classification error, local minima, depth, initialization, edge-of-stability behavior, or batch normalization. Its brief discussion of edge of stability does not measure the behavior named in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports gradient-spike measurements and an experiment that zeroes spiked gradients, but neither tests the listed claim versions. Comparisons of SPAM with other optimizers concern the paper's proposed method and are not rows for these versions. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures gradient spikes and optimizer performance in LLMs. Its suggested connection to edge of stability is speculative: it does not measure sharpness, stability thresholds, or recovery above those thresholds. Its initialization comparisons measure spikes and final perplexity, not the learning speed or trainable depth named in V4. No results test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that gradient spikes are prevalent and detrimental to LLM training, and that SPAM improves performance through momentum reset and spike-aware clipping, including under memory constraints. They suggest an edge-of-stability connection without testing it.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates gradient spikes and optimizer interventions in LLM pre-training and fine-tuning, rather than the listed classification-error, width, depth, initialization, learning-rate-stability, or batch-normalization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that spike frequency is reduced on the cleaner SlimPajama dataset; Scaled Embed and Embed LN reduce spike counts, while other tested mitigation approaches offer little or no improvement. These settings do not test a listed version.

fits_no_version.finding: LLaMA models exhibit gradient spikes associated with small loss bumps during C4 training; removing spiked gradients improves final perplexity for LLaMA-60M. The authors report no catastrophic divergence in these observations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient spikes accompany loss bumps during LLM training, and suppressing them can improve final model performance.

record.problems: The paper describes the gradient-spike removal result as a perplexity improvement but reports its values only in a figure in the supplied text. The theoretical discussion is explicitly preliminary and assumes convexity; the authors note that its gradient-bound assumption may conflict with spikes.
record.rows_left_out: Optimizer comparisons and ablations evaluate SPAM or its components, rather than measuring any behavior named in the listed claim versions. The simulation of moment recovery is not a listed version's behavior. Cited findings are not included.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted or random labels.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep plain convolutional networks.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, sharpness hovering at the stability threshold, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The corrected states concern the listed claim versions; they do not dispute the reported occurrence of gradient spikes. LayerNorm and embedding normalization comparisons do not test batch normalization. Optimizer comparisons and the preliminary convex regret-bound discussion do not establish any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper notes a possible relation to edge of stability but does not measure sharpness, a stability threshold, or recovery from learning rates above that threshold.

rows.subject: LLaMA-60M
rows.operation_detail: Monitored whole-model gradients over the initial 1,000 training steps and identified spikes using GSS(gi) > 50.
rows.measure: Presence of gradient spikes accompanying loss bumps
rows.value: The authors report gradient spikes accompanying loss bumps; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The figure also shows gradient trajectories; no numeric spike count is reported here.
rows.check: Gradient spikes and accompanying loss bumps are observed, but this measure cannot establish any listed version, including V5.
